Hi Priya —

Great to meet you and the Brightline team earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can align the pilot / procurement path: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary workload: interactive customer support + nightly batch embeddings for search
- Expected steady-state volume: 200–400M tokens / month after pilot (peak spikes during launches)
- Performance SLO: P95 latency <= 120ms for short responses (50–150 tokens)

Two asks
1) Can you confirm the preliminary monthly spend band you and finance expect for the first 6 months? On our call you gave a range — I heard ~$80k–$200k / month. Confirming if that maps to your internal PO/commit thresholds.
2) What is the procurement trigger for a PO vs credit card? (finance approval levels, legal review threshold) — this determines whether we route you to standard Hosted API or fast-track a reserved commit/PO onboarding.

Preliminary pricing reference
- Target unit we discussed: target $/1M tokens = $420 (we can show alternatives at different commits and model variants).
- Example: at 300M tokens/mo, that would be roughly $126k/mo on the hosted path; dedicated committed lanes move the unit price down and provide SLA/PO-friendly terms.

Next steps I suggest
- If you can drop the confirmed monthly band and the PO threshold, I'll loop in Neha (Contracts) and Karthik (Solutions) to propose a short procurement path and an estimated rollout cost sheet.

Attaching a short template for budget capture (Brightline_budget_range.xlsx) — fill the green fields if helpful.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Michael

Thanks Michael — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed budget band
- Finance gave an internal target band of $60k–$150k / month for the pilot-to-scale window (months 1–6).
- They prefer to keep initial commit lower and evaluate after 90 days.

Procurement thresholds
- PO required for any vendor spend > $25k / month (Finance sign-off + vendor form).
- Anything < $25k can be put on a corporate card or via a short-term contract, though legal does still review standard terms.

Unit economics tolerance
- Target $/1M tokens ideally <= $450 for our evaluation (we can stretch to $500 for a short pilot if other benefits – caching, KV reuse – are proven).

Questions for Redwood
- Do you offer an interim pricing layer for pilot volumes that keeps unit price around $450 but doesn't require a long-term commit?
- If we hit >$25k/mo, what's Redwood's typical lead time to accept a PO and set up billing (and do you require any SLA addenda)?

I'll fill and send the budget sheet later today. cc'ing infra for any perf/ops notes.

Best —
Priya

Thanks for the context, Michael. Notes from Contracts/Finance side below.

Quick answers
- PO acceptance lead time: standard intake is 5–7 business days once we have the PO + completed vendor form. If SLA/contract redlines are requested, add 7–10 business days.
- Temporary pilot pricing: we can offer a pilot pricing commitment (45 days) that sets unit at $445/1M tokens for volumes up to 250M tokens/month without a long-term commit — this is an exceptionable SKU and requires a short SOW and billing note.
- Card vs PO: Anything <= $25k/mo can go on card/self-serve. We'll need a PO + vendor form for > $25k and Finance issues the invoice cadence.

Attachments & next steps
- I attached a SOC2 evidence summary we usually provide to customers starting PO intake (SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf).
- Michael: please confirm whether Brightline will accept a 45-day pilot SOW at $445/1M up to 250M tokens. If yes, I'll prepare the SOW template and vendor intake checklist and accelerate the PO lane.

Procurement tip (for Karthik / Sales ops)
- When one-off pilot pricing is used, flag the deal in HubSpot with property: pilot_pricing_exception = true and tag contracts owner to avoid re-pricing on renewal.
